MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron sits in a "multi-token proper-name continuation" circuit: it is driven most negatively by highly predictable next-words in place/organization names (e.g. "Canary/Channel" before "Islands", "Government of India", "Dorset-street"), while its positive/max side fires on the less-predictable continuation token inside a place-name, address or model-spec string (e.g. "Saurashtra-Ver-aval", "El Dorado Acres Homes", "WAINGANGA EXP").

This neuron fires on the highly predictable word that completes a fixed collocation or idiom — typically the head noun ("apologize for the ~inconvenience~", "5-game ~suspension~", "changing our ~name~", "don't lose ~air~") or the infinitival "to" following a noun that licenses it ("pressure … to accept", "change the end date to get round this"); it is strongly suppressed on similar filler/function words in vaguer set phrases ("come up with some sort of", "deal to avoid", "and take necessary action").

Fires on the predicate/head word a few tokens into a contrastive or qualifying clause (typically after "but", "although", "and even", "only"), i.e. the verb or preposition that completes the contrast ("banks **have** held steady", "notice them **when**", "were **instead** explained", "routinely **bring** along", "but I see a councillor **at** school"); the same kinds of verbs in plain non-contrastive assertions ("there **is**", "does **affect**", "accr**ue**") strongly suppress it.
